share_verdict: The mill kept the flour. It threw away the germ.

ingredients.name: stone-ground whole wheat
ingredients.function: the whole grain, bran, germ and endosperm, because there was no way to separate them at scale

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.function: hydration; whole-grain flour drinks more than refined

ingredients.name: ghee
ingredients.quantity_modern: 1 tsp in the dough, more to finish
ingredients.function: softens the crumb and carries fat-soluble nutrients from the bran

method_reconstructed: Grind the wheat on a stone quern, cool and slow. The germ oil stays in the flour.
Bring the flour together with warm water into a soft dough; rest it.
Cook on a hot griddle, then finish directly over embers so it puffs.
contested_points: Several flatbreads are named in the medieval literature, rotikā, maṇḍaka, pūrikā and others, and mapping each onto a modern bread is not clean.
Wheat was a regional staple, not a national one. In much of the south and east the everyday flatbread was millet or rice, not wheat.

changed.from: stone-ground whole wheat, ground within days of eating
changed.to: roller-milled atta, often with the germ removed and bran added back
changed.driver: roller mills separate bran, germ and endosperm cleanly and cheaply, which is what makes flour keep for months instead of weeks. The germ is the part that goes rancid, and the part with most of the fat-soluble vitamins

changed.from: wheat as one flatbread grain among many, regionally
changed.to: wheat and rice as the default grains nationally
changed.driver: procurement and the public distribution system were built around wheat and rice; millets fell out of the supply chain and then off the plate

ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat, or the coarsest chakki atta your kirana stocks
Salt, optional, the old versions largely did without
steps: If you can get whole wheat berries, have them ground at a chakki and use the flour within a fortnight. That single change is most of the difference.
Bring the flour together with warm water, knead five minutes, rest 20.
Roll thin, cook on a hot tawa until it blisters, then hold it over the flame until it balloons.
Coarser flour makes a heavier roti that tears rather than folds. That is what it is meant to be.
